★ Request
Believe stands up

During training—
Lately, we've been focusing primarily on building speed and endurance.

I will finish before the sun sets completely.
So, there is no problem.

Understood.
No changes to the uphill slope training afterward today, correct?

...Even if I pressed further, it was clear she wouldn't let me help.
Accepting that that was her stance, I silently watch over her.

Other than that, maybe it would be fine to shift the timing
for pushing to top speed a bit earlier, but...
In that case... rather than forcing any more speed work, it would be better to shift toward building explosive power. I'll fine-tune the routine.

She coordinates her training details with me properly like this.
That in itself must be proof that she accepts me as a "work" partner.

Looking closely, some of the bricks on the flowerbed really have crumbled.
Fixing this alone is going to take quite a bit of time.

As her Trainer, shouldn't we be opening up more to each other by now...?
While wrestling with that thought, I casually glance out the window—
...I need to be careful.
Haah, haah... haah—!

I'm fixing the flowerbed.
Because I was asked to.

...I think I can hold on even if I push the timing earlier.
However, it will be close to the limit.

(...Trainer looked pretty uncomfortable just now.
Did I... sound too cold again?)

...Well, I'm heading back.
Good work today.

Watching Believe walk away, I ponder the meaning
behind the sigh she let out just a moment ago.

...She leaves without lingering, and I see her off without
even managing any small talk. It's still like this every single day.

Did my offering to help, or even standing by and watching,
actually get in her way...?
That won't be necessary. I have enough hands.

—Is this good enough?
......

I had her run the final 3 furlongs near top speed, but...
her pace was steady all the way to the goal, and the lap times were solid.

No, that's fine.
This is my job.

...I suppose I should rest for now.
—Rest...

Only the quiet, steady sounds of brick repair echo through the air.
As I watch on without anything I can do to help—

It appears she finished repairing the flowerbed
right on schedule, just as she said she would.
However...—

For some reason, Believe was outside the window.
I thought for sure she had headed straight back to the dorm after training...

Thank you very much.
—Well, good work today.

She trusts me as a "work" partner. There's no doubt about that.
Yet... our relationship remains thoroughly businesslike.

—The sun is truly beginning to set now. It will be dark soon.
She must have her own post-training care, laundry, and meals to attend to.

The cracks where the bricks join keep standing out no matter what...
Was it a lack of materials after all... No, there must've been a better way...
(Scrape, scrape—clack, clack...)

After training.
I thought I'd check in on her with some words of encouragement, but—

—Phew.
...How was my speed?
